observations.content:

observations.title: Map portable structural profile library extension points
observations.content:
**What**: Completed read-only architecture research for a custom structural profile library, with mandatory desktop/web parity; no implementation decision or source changes authorized.
**Why**: User requested implementation analysis, pros, cons, opportunities and improvements, then explicitly required web support.
**Where**: crates/doc/src/frame.rs (ProfileSpec and MemberProfile), crates/engine/src/cmd/frame.rs, crates/io/src/catalog.rs, crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_library.rs:108, apps/solidcraft-web/src/files.rs, upstream issue #4003 and open PR #7405.
**Learned**: Existing seven built-in profile families plus sketch-based members are not a user catalog. Existing material/appearance catalog conventions include qualified identities, revisions and provenance. Web already uses in-memory VFS with host OPFS persistence and localStorage fallback; IndexedDB is used for file handles, not a profile database. Existing library UI explicitly disables interactive import on wasm, confirmed by parent spot read. Recommend (proposal only) portable JSON presets first, reuse VFS/OPFS rather than introduce IndexedDB/SQLite by default, embed selected profile definitions in designs from first release, explicit revisions/updates, then bounded self-contained sketch sections. Parent spot-checked frame serialization and web files. Native/web geometric equality and browser persistence were not tested. Upstream #4003 plans a profile library; #7405 is an open filesystem-based parts library, not an implemented structural catalog. GPL and commercial CAD templates/data are forbidden; public availability is not redistribution permission.

observations.title: Require DXF and DWG profile import evaluation
observations.content:
**What**: User requires evaluating import of existing .dxf or .dwg cross-sections into the planned reusable profile library rather than redrawing sketches.
**Why**: User explicitly said: "Tambien debemos tener en cuenta importar .dxf o .dwg si tengo perfiles diseñados en autocad o OpencadStudio poder usarlos sin tener que hacer el croquis de cero".
**Where**: Read-only profile library architecture analysis for SolidCraft, mandatory desktop/web parity.
**Learned**: Existing user-owned drawing import is a requested workflow; DXF and DWG support must be evaluated separately and no equivalent native/web support has been promised. Do not automate commercial CAD or use its output as committed reference fixtures; use original analytic fixtures for implementation tests.

observations.title: Confirm existing DXF-to-frame profile workflow
observations.content:
**What**: Confirmed SolidCraft already documents importing a DXF with sketch.insert_dxf and using that sketch as frame.member profile_sketch; this avoids redrawing but does not yet create a reusable catalog entry.
**Why**: User requested reusing existing DXF/DWG profiles from AutoCAD or OpenCAD Studio with mandatory web support.
**Where**: docs/frames.md:12-22, crates/io/src/dxf.rs:1-65, crates/io/src/lib.rs:946.
**Learned**: Existing parser accepts ASCII DXF and explicitly rejects binary DXF; handles common entities, splines/ellipses and expanded blocks within supported implementation limits. INSUNITS conversion supports a subset (in, ft, mm, cm, m), defaulting other values to mm; import workflow should explicitly confirm unknown or missing units rather than silently infer scale. Existing format test rejects a.dwg. Proposal: add import/validate/choose region/origin/save snapshot workflow, with DXF prioritized; direct DWG requires a separately evaluated legal and wasm-compatible reader/conversion solution, not a promised equivalent capability. No tests run or source changes made.

observations.title: Define strict DXF profile import architecture proposal
observations.content:
**What**: Reviewed focused explorer findings and proposed a versioned self-contained custom-section contract using existing Region2/Loop2/Seg2 geometry through explicit format conversion, with strict diagnostic-first DXF import; proposal only, no source changes.
**Why**: User authorized continuing architecture analysis and defining the custom-section contract with mandatory browser support and reuse of DXF/DWG drawings.
**Where**: crates/io/src/dxf.rs, crates/engine/src/cmd/sketch_import.rs:45-129, crates/geom/src/profile.rs:11-46,578-583; parent spot-read latter two files.
**Learned**: Current DXF read output loses units/layers/handles; units may default to mm; OCS/Z silently ignored; arbitrary rational spline knots/weights are not retained, partial ellipses and some block transforms become sampled fit splines. Current add_geometry welds all defining points (including centers/control points), truncates spline points and ignores add_curve errors; cannot serve as strict accepted-profile proof unchanged. Proposed first delivery accepts validated planar ASCII DXF line/arc/circle sections (expanded supported blocks only when fidelity established), reports/rejects unsupported selected geometry instead of silent losses, separates source inspection from final import, no automatic geometry repair, confirms ambiguous units, embeds selected normalized region and revision in document. Preserve generic sketch.insert_dxf behavior; no kernel changes proposed. Region2 serde exists but is not by itself a validated or stable public interchange contract. Proposed external format needs explicit versioned mapping, complexity limits and geometry validation; declared/estimated approximation must not be called certified error. Direct DWG remains unresolved; no tests or browser checks executed.

observations.title: Restrict imported profiles to one connected material region without blocks
observations.content:
**What**: User explicitly disallows DXF blocks and disconnected material islands in imported profiles; closed continuous boundaries may define holes, but three concentric circles must be rejected.
**Why**: User correction verbatim: "No permitamos bloques, debemos admitir \"perfiles\" con contornos continuos e interconestados (perfiles con agujeros) pero no islas sueltas dentro de un perfil (por ejemplo 3 circulos concentricos) entiendes la idea?"
**Where**: Proposed SolidCraft profile library DXF acceptance contract, desktop and web; no implementation yet.
**Learned**: Valid profile = one connected material region with one outer closed contour and zero or more holes; a hole need not physically connect its boundary to the outer boundary. Two concentric circles form a valid annulus; three create an isolated inner disk and must be rejected, not silently discard it. Multiple nonnested holes can be valid. Blocks must not be auto-expanded in the profile workflow; generic importer behavior remains outside this correction.

Objective: reusable structural sections on desktop and web. Branch: `feat/profile-library-dxf`; baseline: `9cba66c1`. Local-only: no push, issue or PR publication.

First-delivery proposal accepted in context: ASCII DXF first; direct DWG remains separately unverified and is not promised in this implementation.
S4. Topology and block correction: "No permitamos bloques, debemos admitir \"perfiles\" con contornos continuos e interconestados (perfiles con agujeros) pero no islas sueltas dentro de un perfil (por ejemplo 3 circulos concentricos) entiendes la idea?". S5. Implementation destination selected explicitly: "Solo local en mi fork, sin publicar".
S6. Environment permission: "Autorizar la instalación" for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `trunk`, writing to `/home/max/.rustup` and `/home/max/.cargo`.

observations.content:
Goal: Implement and verify the first portable structural profile library delivery for SolidCraft with strict DXF import, custom hole-tolerant topology, and full desktop/web parity.
Instructions: User explicitly required local-only development on their fork (sclMAX/solidcraft) without upstream publication or PR creation, strict ASCII DXF without blocks, single connected material region (holes permitted, concentric islands rejected), and verified browser parity.
Discoveries:
1. SolidCraft's generic DXF reader flattens coordinates and defaults missing units to mm; strict profile import needed a separate analytic reader rejecting blocks, non-coplanar coordinates and ambiguous units.
2. Section topology requires strict analytic predicates; three concentric circles produce an isolated disk and are rejected atomically.
3. Persistent document loading (Document::from_json) previously lacked profile validation, allowing hand-edited designs to bypass catalog rules; fixed by enforcing MAX_SAVED_PROFILES (128), key/name equality and revision verification.
4. Browser file picker routes DXF/catalog JSON to DOM file upload and downloads respectively via VFS/OPFS; Firefox verification confirmed end-to-end import, preview, member creation and reload persistence.
Accomplished:
- Implemented strict DXF reader (crates/io/src/profile_dxf.rs) and connected section validator (crates/doc/src/frame_section.rs).
- Added portable catalog format solidcraft-profiles/1 (crates/io/src/profile_catalog.rs).
- Added frame_profiles to Document with immutable member snapshots and hostile-open validation (crates/doc/src/document.rs).
- Implemented typed engine commands frame.profile.library, import_dxf, inspect_dxf, save, import, export (crates/engine/src/cmd/frame_library.rs and schema).
- Built shared desktop/web UI dialog Saved Profiles and member selector (crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs_profile_library.rs).
- All gates passed: cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings (0 warnings), unit/integration tests, wasm32 check and Firefox real runtime probe.
- Created commit f6595831 and pushed branch feat/profile-library-dxf to origin (sclMAX/solidcraft).
Next Steps:

- Expand profile library to support custom sketched contours and T/Z families.
- Add cut list and miter/trim treatments (#4003).
